title: Frontend: Deep Clone Object
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Deep Clone Object. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({value,cycle?}). Deep-clone a JSON object/array graph. If cycle is true, a root self-reference and shared aliases are added before cloning. Return {equal,distinct,nestedDistinct,cyclePreserved,aliasPreserved}. equal compares the original JSON value, excluding injected links. Do not mutate the supplied value.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Use a source-to-clone map and register each clone before traversing children, so cycles terminate and shared references remain shared.
alternativeApproaches: Preserve property descriptors and explain why copying getters can trigger side effects if implemented by reading values.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Self-cycle; shared child; Date/Map policy.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
